text:
Priya: Heads-up — VaultBank wants a short POC but they're strict: all inference, logs, and model artifacts must remain inside the EU for EU tenants; explicitly no US sub-processors or telemetry outbound to US.
Marco: Understood. Do we have an up-to-date sub-processor list + cert links we can hand them (SOC2 / ISO)? Legal wants the chain.
Jenna: Current infra: EU primary in Dublin (GCP), DR in Paris (Azure). APAC in Tokyo (AWS ap-northeast-1). Note: some monitoring and error-trace vendors default to US endpoints (Honeycomb, Datadog).
Priya: They said zero tolerance for US telemetry egress. Can we promise that for a 10-business-day POC?
Viktor: Short answer: we can for Dedicated or Private deployments. Hosted product uses central control plane services in the US (billing + some feature telemetry). For a Hosted POC we'd need a legal exception.
Marco: Customer prefers Hosted pricing/credit for POC. If we require Dedicated, they'll ask for compensating credits. Any quick cost delta?
Jenna: Rough estimate: EU Dedicated POC with 2x A40-equivalent GPUs reserved: ~€5k for two weeks (includes network, temporary ops). If we need Private with customer-managed VPC + KMS in-region, add ~€3-4k setup fee and extra ops days.
Priya: They want a Hosted-like UX but EU-only for two weeks. Is there a minimal config we can flip to simulate Hosted while keeping everything in EU?
Viktor: Yes — we can provision a temporary EU-dedicated namespace and disable external telemetry and cross-region failover. Example config we use for these POCs:
```
routing_policy: "REGION_PIN_EU"
telemetry_mode: "DISABLED_EXTERNAL"
subprocess_exclude: ["honeycomb", "datadog", "sentry"]
kms_region: "europe-west1"
allow_cross_border_failover: false
```
Marco: Good. What about provider certs for those subprocessors we still use (e.g., CDN, storage snapshot vendor)? They need cert chains and ISO docs per vendor.
Jenna: We'll produce a subproc matrix with links to each vendor's ISO/SOC pages. For EU-only POC we'll ensure any optional agents that contact vendors are disabled. For vendors without EU-hosted options, we'll mark them as excluded.
Priya: Client also asked: if EU capacity hits max, will requests ever be routed to US as fallback? They want a definitive 'no' during POC.
Viktor: We can commit in writing: no automatic cross-border fallback for the POC term. DR is a separate conversation; if DR is needed it's manual and requires signed exception.
Marco: Can we get a short contract snippet we can put in the SOW?
Jenna: Draft clause: "During the POC term, Redwood will enforce EU region pinning for the tenant, disable specified external telemetry and exclude listed sub-processors. No automatic cross-border processing will occur without prior written consent."
Priya: Perfect. Also need SOC2 pack and an ops handoff timeline post-POC — customer wants to know when we can hand to their platform team.
Viktor: SOC2 docs: we can share redacted reports via our compliance portal. Ops handoff: if POC goes well, we can do a 3-business-day handoff after close; runbooks and playbook review included.
Marco: Who is point for compliance and runbooks? I'll put contact in the deck.
Jenna: Compliance: maria@redwood-example.com (SOC2/ISO contact). SolutionsEng for runbooks: eng-solutions@redwood-example.com.
infra-bot: Ticket INFRA-9001 created for EU-dedicated POC provisioning (ETA 4 business days). Reminder set: follow up in 72 hours.
Priya: I'll propose two options to VaultBank: 1) Hosted POC (fastest) — note: cannot meet EU-only telemetry requirement without exception; 2) EU Dedicated POC (meets residency + telemetry exclusion) — estimated cost ~€5k, 4-5 business day lead. I'll ask for their preference and attach the draft clause and subproc matrix when ready.
Marco: If they push back on cost, we can offer a partial credit in exchange for a 30-day evaluation and feedback session.
Viktor: I'll assemble the subproc matrix and mark each vendor: 'EU-hosted', 'US-only', or 'excluded'. ETA EOD.
Priya: Thanks — looping in legal and solutionseng when I reply. :thumbsup:
